answer: Each agent must anchor its identity in a hardware enclave whose lattice-based keypair is bound to a unique physical unclonable function, making cheap mass registration as futile as carving a sonnet into marble. Consensus admits new identities only after a verifiable delay and randomized ocean of peer challenges, so a single operator cannot flood the registry with cloned nodes. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
